newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN pays $144 mln from oil-for-food to Iraq victims.
newsitem.headline: UN pays $144 mln from oil-for-food to Iraq victims.

text.p: The U.N. Gulf War reparations body said on Wednesday that it had paid $144 million to the governments of 57,636 successful claimants, its first payments funded by revenues from the "oil-for-food" agreement with Iraq.

The U.N. Compensation Commission said the money had been transferred to 63 governments for distribution to 57,636 people who proved they were forced to leave Kuwait or Iraq or who lost up to $100,000.
Diplomats and legal analysts said the payments were expected to restore faith in the reparations scheme, which was set up by the Security Council in 1991.

But the commission needs huge sums to compensate individuals, corporations and governments which have filed claims valued at more than $220 billion against Baghdad for losses directly due to the Iraq's invasion of Kuwait in August 1990 and its seven-month occupation, they said.
The Geneva-based body said the payments were funded by its 30 per cent share of revenue from the sale of Iraqi crude oil sold under the "oil-for-food" deal implemented since December.

The deal allows Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to buy humanitarian goods for its people to ease the impact of stringent sanctions. No goods have arrived yet in Iraq, according to the United Nations and Baghdad.

"Claimants are to receive an initial payment of up to $2,500 each," the commission said in its statement. "For those whose actual award amounts exceed this figure, additional payments are to be made later."

The largest group of successful claimants in the departure category being paid -- randomly selected by computer -- were 23,334 Egyptian migrant workers forced to leave Kuwait or Iraq, it said. They were awarded a total of $58.3 million.

Sri Lankan and Indian workers were to receive $15.9 million and $15.5 million respectively, followed by Bangladeshi workers ($11.3 million) and Kuwaiti citizens forced to leave their homeland ($11.3 million).
A total of 1,061 Kuwaitis who proved losses of up to $100,000 were to receive $2.6 million under the pay out, along with 1,101 Pakistanis getting a total of $2.7 million for such losses.
The commission, funded largely by donations and seized Iraqi assets, previously paid $13.4 million to 3,966 people who proved the death of close relative or their serious injury to themselves.
